title: Privacy Policy (Datenschutzerklärung)
intro: This page explains in plain words what data Party Watcher collects, why, on which legal basis (GDPR / DSGVO), who receives it and what rights you have. The Russian version prevails.
controllerH: 1. Who is responsible for the data

s2.h: 2. What data we process and why
s2.body:
• Account: username, email, password hash (the password itself is not stored) and the date it was last changed, settings, follows, role. Needed so that you can use your account — performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
  • What you publish: chat messages, room and stream titles, profile design, streams, recordings and clips, support requests and reports (and screenshots, if you attached them). When a live stream is reported, its last ~30 seconds are saved — only the administration can see them. Needed for these features to work — performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)).
  • Security: IP address, country from IP, browser and device type, a random browser id and an anonymised fingerprint of device characteristics (graphics card, cores, screen, time zone), linked to the account. Needed to protect the service and people from hacking, spam, inflation and ban evasion (IP and device bans) — our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR; § 25(2) TDDDG — the service cannot be provided securely without it). You can object to this processing (section 6).
  • Account history: previous emails and usernames, when the stream channel was created, when the password and the main device were changed — from which IP and device. Needed to return the account to its owner if it is stolen — our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Only administrators can see it.
  • Sign-in sessions: device, IP address, country, sign-in time and last activity (updated at most once an hour) — to show you in your profile where the account is open and let you end a session that is not yours — legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)). The account’s first device is marked as the main one.
  • Visit statistics: device, browser, country, pages viewed and number of requests — only if you clicked “Accept statistics” in the banner (consent, Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR; § 25(1) TDDDG). Without consent only anonymous overall server load counters are kept.
  • Emails: email confirmation, password reset, support replies — performance of a contract.
  • Streamer page in search engines: the public channel page (nickname, avatar, description, title and frame of the live stream, follower count) may be shown in Google, Yandex and Bing if the channel streams regularly. For this we count how many streams of 30+ minutes the channel had in a month. The streamer can turn this off at any time in the studio (the “Show my channel in search engines” checkbox) — the page then leaves search results. Channels with 18+ streams are not shown in search. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in the site and its streamers being found (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

There is no advertising, no selling of data, no ad profiling and no third-party trackers on the site.

s3.body:
• token — signing in (necessary).
  • pw_lang — chosen language (necessary for the site to work).
  • pw_dev — browser id and device fingerprint for security and bans (see section 2).
  • pw_consent — your choice in the statistics banner.
  • localStorage pw_age18 — a note that you confirmed you are 18+ on this device (18+ rooms and streams), so we don't ask again and can show 18+ streams in the streams directory; for accounts it is also stored in the account (necessary to protect minors).
  • localStorage pw_chat_rules — a note that you accepted a channel's chat rules, so we don't ask again (necessary for the chat to work).
  • Browser localStorage — theme, window and button positions, volume, profile cache so pages open faster. It is not shared with third parties.

s4.body:
We use processors (Auftragsverarbeiter) — only to the extent needed for the site to work:

  • Cloudflare — site delivery and attack protection (all traffic, including your IP address, passes through their network).
  • Oracle Cloud — the site server and database (data centre in India, Mumbai).
  • GitHub — storage of database backups. Backups are encrypted before upload (AES-256) and only we hold the key: GitHub cannot read them.
  • Resend — sending emails (recipient address and email text).
  • DeepL — machine translation of news (only the news text is sent).
  • Twitch — list of stream categories (your data is not sent).

Search engines (Google, Microsoft Bing, Yandex) are not processors but independent recipients: when a streamer whose channel is shown in search starts or ends a stream, we send them the address of their page (via the Google Indexing API and IndexNow) so that search results update sooner. Only the address of the public page is sent — no viewer data.

The streamer and their moderators only see your username and what you do on the channel: chat messages (including through the streamer's programs and OBS overlay), your follow and its date, rewards and the text you add to them, bans and timeouts. They do not see your email, IP address, country or device.

Some recipients are outside the EU (USA, India). Transfers are based on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Art. 46 GDPR) and, where applicable, the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Art. 45 GDPR).

When you open a room with a YouTube, Twitch, VK Video or Kodik video, the player loads directly from their servers: they receive your IP address and browser data and process it under their own policies.

s5.body:
• Visit statistics — 120 days.
  • An account's IP addresses and devices (security) — 1 year after the last visit.
  • An unconfirmed sign-up — 30 minutes, then deleted. If the daily email limit is used up, the sign-up waits in a queue for up to 3 days, and the link in an email from the queue works for 8 hours.
  • Stream and room chat messages — 3 days (the streamer can delete them earlier with “Clear chat”, a room's chat is deleted together with the room).
  • Account data and published content — as long as the account exists (clips and stream recordings — for a limited time).
  • A sign-in session — until you sign out or end it in your profile, but no longer than 7 days.
  • Account history — as long as the account exists.
  • Deleting the account from the profile: the account is frozen at once and deleted together with its data and files after 3 days (earlier if support deletes it); signing in with the password within these 3 days cancels the deletion. Your messages in other people’s stream chats remain without your name. A snapshot of the account’s activity in the day before the request (messages, sign-ins, rooms created) is kept in the support request for another 30 days after deletion — to look into possible violations (legitimate interest).
  • Support requests — as long as needed to answer and resolve them; attached screenshots and stream recordings attached to reports — 90 days.
  • Database backups (encrypted) — 7 days, then deleted.

s6.body:
At any time you can: find out what data we hold about you (Art. 15 GDPR), correct it (Art. 16), delete it (Art. 17), restrict processing (Art. 18), receive it in a machine-readable format (Art. 20), object to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21) and withdraw your consent to statistics — with the button below, without any effect on how the site works.

You can also delete your account yourself: profile → “Security” → “Delete account”. For anything else, write to support@partywatcher.de from your account's email — we will reply within a month.

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, for example: Der Landesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg, Lautenschlagerstraße 20, 70173 Stuttgart.

s7.body: The service is intended for people aged 18 and over. We may update this policy — the current version is always on this page, with the date at the top.
